rounds.text: Timex Group India Ltd trades at a prohibitive valuation across multiple metrics, including a price-to-earnings ratio of 59.9x [E1] and an elevated price-to-book multiple of 70.95x [E2], which towers over the sector benchmark P/B of 2.76x [E7]. A discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 347 per share against a market price of Rs 530, resulting in a stark negative margin of safety of -52.6% [E42, E43]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price already bakes in an aggressive 23.9% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case assumption of 18.0% [E44]. Compounding these valuation concerns, promoter shareholding has experienced a sharp contraction, dropping by 23.93 percentage points from 74.93% in September 2023 to 51.00% by June 2026 [E38], while the company notably distributes a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reporting repeated profits [E4, E61]. Additional red flags from Screener warn that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E62], and rules-based screens flag that earnings growth is actively decelerating alongside a rich valuation warning [E69, E71]. Conceded: [E13], [E19], [E32].
